content:
ashley: starting a config-only deploy to canary now — routing + batching + timeouts. change_id cfg-20260319-17. canary = 3 hosts (~5%) for 20m. pinging @samir @mike for quick checks

deploy-bot: QUEUED: cfg-20260319-17 -> canary group=eng-inference-canary targets=3 perc=5 status=STARTING

samir: oncall -> running quick smoke: curl /health and a sample generate against canary endpoint, will post results

mike: skimmed the diff. main changes I care about: reduce max_batch_size 32->16, request_timeout 8s->5s, routing preference set to prefer_low_latency, added per-customer concurrency cap 50. looks safe but watch p95

jen: can you paste the config snippet? want to see exact values

ashley: sure, snippet below (config-only):
```
routing:
  prefer_low_latency: true
  fallback_policy: standard
batching:
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
  max_batch_size: 16
timeouts:
  request: 5s
  kv_cache_eviction: 120s
limits:
  concurrency_per_customer: 50
```

qa-bot: CANARY-SMOKE: 200 OK for /health, sample-gen median latency 140ms (+10ms vs baseline), p95 420ms (-20ms), errors=0/500 samples, cost_estimate_per_token -12%

sre-oncall: watching error budget. alert threshold set to 0.5% errors and 2x baseline latency. I have dashboard pinned: https://internal.redwood/dashboards/cfg-20260319-17

samir: logs look clean so far, no KV evictions spiking in the first 10m. tails show consistent KV hit rate ~92%

mike: question — should we pin model variant for this canary? the quant kernels behave differently with smaller batches. i'd prefer model pin to llama-3-quant-v1.3 for canary

ashley: good call, pinning now

deploy-bot: PIN_CREATED: change_id=cfg-20260319-17 model_pin=llama-3-quant-v1.3 scope=canary

qa-bot: extended smoke at +15m: samples still passing, no increased error rate, latency stable. cost simulation shows estimated 10-14% token cost savings under current traffic mix

sre-oncall: no alerts. rolling window error rate 0.08% last 15m. p95 stable.

jen: canary looks healthy to me. recommend promote to stable but keep the per-customer concurrency cap for 6 hours post-promotion as a safety valve

mike: +1 to staged promotion with a conservative auto-scale for the first hour

ashley: promoting to stable in 10m. release notes draft coming. adding a changelog entry under "runtime config tweaks"

deploy-bot: PROMOTION_SCHEDULED: cfg-20260319-17 -> stable at 1832401500 (in 10m). post-promote checks enabled: health, error_rate, latency_regressions

ashley: release notes snippet for docs: "Config-only update: lowered request timeout from 8s to 5s, reduced max_batch_size to 16 to improve latency tail, enabled prefer_low_latency routing, added per-customer concurrency cap (50) to protect noisy tenants. Expected token cost reduction ~10-14% for common workloads."

samir: leaving a note to SRE rotations to watch for any spike in 5xxs or rate-limited customers. I'll keep an eye for the next 2 hours

mike: thumbs up :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: COMPLETE: cfg-20260319-17 promoted -> stable. all post-promote checks PASS. changelist: routing,batching,timeouts,limits

ashley: thanks everyone — closing this thread. will follow up in release notes and changelog page.
